construction.block_graph: r by r grid, k=r^2 R44AS blocks, all sharing the same pivot x
construction.nonpivot_variables: five per block, disjoint between blocks
construction.connector: for every grid edge {u,v}, add the complete 12-clause orbit under the R44BP signed permutation pi of the seed (x1_u OR not x3_v OR x4_u)

sat_and_structure.binary_congruence: singleton classes only; connectors have width 3 and base siblings have no nontrivial binary SCC equivalences
sat_and_structure.transport_exists: blockwise R44BP pi maps the full connector orbit set into itself

treewidth_escape.minor: Contract each connected five-variable local block in a child primal graph to one vertex. Every grid edge has at least one connector crossing its two blocks, so the contracted graph contains the r by r grid as a minor.
treewidth_escape.consequence: Child primal treewidth is unbounded as r grows; in particular this family is not contained in any fixed bounded-treewidth SAT class.
treewidth_escape.source_note: Uses standard graph-theoretic facts that treewidth is minor-monotone and square grids have treewidth growing linearly with side length.

r44bc_escape.consequence: For sufficiently large r, delta* is far above floor(log2 S), so the R44BC low-maxdef terminal does not apply.

theorem_effect.result: The R44BX path-family bounded-treewidth terminal escape is removed while preserving connectedness, congruence rigidity, strict branch descent, and growing transport/deviation support.
theorem_effect.not_claimed: No search-hardness theorem and no P-vs-NP conclusion. The repeated global pi generator may still be polynomially discoverable.

next_exact_question: Can the repeated global pi action on this high-treewidth congruence-rigid family be recovered by a deterministic polynomial structural invariant, or can the blockwise generators be coupled nonuniformly so that safe relation discovery itself becomes the next exact obstruction without reintroducing a polynomial terminal?
